Borzna Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chernihiv Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Borzna's Jewish community, destroyed in 1648, did not return until the mid-18th century, growing to 1,516 (12.1 percent) by 1897; interwar rabbis included the Lubavitcher Hasid Avrohom-Yitshok Glazman, who is buried at this cemetery. The community withstood pogroms beginning in 1881, and a wave carried out by the Volunteer Army in September 1919 destroyed the synagogue and killed 20 Jews. Sources differ on the WWII death toll — published figures cite about 119 shot in November 1941, while a 1990s study found the actual number to be 168, a discrepancy noted here rather than resolved. The Jewish community was officially re-established in 1995.
